scope: One representative formal output per cohort; five sampled frames plus full video/audio decoding and signal checks

00-baseline.observation: Reference subject, clothing and room remain consistent in the five sampled frames. A head turn is visible near the middle sample.

01-pdd8.observation: Reference subject and background remain recognizable. Head-turn direction and expression differ from Base50 in the sampled frames.

02-vsa.observation: Subject and background remain recognizable; expression and motion differ from the dense eight-step sample.

03-qad-native-fp4.observation: Sampled frames preserve the subject and room; head motion and mouth shapes differ from earlier model configurations.

04-ulysses.observation: No obvious structural corruption in sampled face, clothing or background; output pixels and generated audio differ from group 3.

05-head-232.observation: No obvious structural corruption in sampled frames; face, clothing and background remain consistent.

06-cuda-graph.observation: Sampled appearance matches group 5; decoded formal video and audio hashes match group 5 exactly.

07-vae-output.observation: Sampled face, clothing and room remain consistent; minor rendering differences from group 6 are visible. No black or empty sampled frames.

overall_observation: No obvious structural failure in sampled frames. All decoded audio samples are finite and non-silent; no sample reaches full scale. These checks do not establish equal perceptual quality across model configurations.

limitations: Signal checks detect structural failures, not speech or audiovisual quality.
Frame sampling does not establish full temporal continuity or lip synchronization.
Generative output differences across configurations are not treated as quality scores.
